dedupe_keys.name: cyclestreets cycle journey planner and api

description: CycleStreets is a cycle journey planner built by cyclists for cyclists, created by Simon Nuttall and Martin Lucas-Smith of Cambridge. It plans fastest, quietest and balanced cycle routes in the UK and some other areas, knows Sustrans routes and avoids hills. The CycleStreets API version 2 is a JSON interface to the routing engine and other components: journey planning, leisure routes, isochrones, a batch routes matrix, a geocoder, the Photomap of cycling infrastructure photos, points of interest, collisions data, traffic counts data, infrastructure locations with a schema, low-traffic neighbourhood data and map downloads. Map data come from OpenStreetMap under the Open Database License, so routes inherit that licence. Access: an API key is needed and granted at CycleStreets' option; a free tier allows up to 10,000 km of route planning a day for free apps and 5,000 km for paid apps, and SLA contracts cover commercial and bulk use. Caveats: routing is best in the UK, and bulk use needs a contract. It supports cycle route choice, accessibility and network flow studies and is used as a routing source by the Propensity to Cycle Tool catalogued here, alongside OSMnx.
